corrections: Require isolated Python, its main/only kernel thread, default Python/kernel SIGCHLD and no SA_NOCLDWAIT before spawning.
Inspect the Linux x86-64 signal action through a read-only rt_sigaction request; refuse other ABI/hosts and visible unexpected signal handlers.
Serialize owned child lifetimes and keep distinct kernel-reaped and ownership-lost records.
Before numeric group signalling, require kernel WNOWAIT child evidence and matching session/group under the unchanged exclusive-reaping context.
Use direct kernel waitpid status rather than Popen's unavailable-status fallback. ECHILD fails without manufacturing a zero exit code.
Ownership/status loss refuses signalling while remaining reader and pipe closes are still attempted.
additionalCoverage: Default and auto-reap context rejection, changed context, wrong parent, foreign child and wrong group/session
True zero, nonzero and signalled statuses, untracked Popen returncode, stopped/unexpected status and wait timeout
Ownership loss during capture, exact-limit EOF, cleanup-only failure, spawn-gate release and lifetime serialization
Injected raw-syscall argument layout and failure handling without invoking a native syscall
limitations: No actual Linux syscall, process group or kernel status was exercised; compatibility and enforcement remain unproven.
The host must remain a dedicated trusted isolated supervisor, not a general multithreaded application.
External hard deadlines for spawn/close, target introspection compatibility, complete cgroup clearance and protected production baselines are still required.
The outstanding fixture correction only affects reproducing the old signal case; it must not cause the 44 passing tests to be rerun or be mistaken for a product fix.
The independent a1 review was followed by this local correction pass; no second independent review is claimed.
Private source and raw logs are not part of this documentation-only commit.
